posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
With Oblivaeon closer to actually being in our hands, what’s next for the Video Game afterwards?

With Sentinels of Earth Prime on the horizon, that would seem to be the next step. But, let’s be honest. When has Green Ronin delivered a product in a timely manner? They’re a small company, so I understand and forgive them. But it could be literally years before we see any new “official” Sentinels decks.

There is, however, an incredible “non-official” expansion with currently roughly 17 heroes, 11 villains, and 8 environments. Not to mention 5 additional heroes, 3 new environments and 4 new villains currently being tested for the 4th “season”. Sidenote: Drift is amazing. The art mirrors Adams in that it started out rough but became something to admire as the project aged.

I believe, whole heartedly, that what TOSX and his peeps created, should be given strong consideration for the privilege of being called an Official expansion with the Abstract Comics imprint standing side by side with Sentinel Comics and Earth Prime.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I think it's more: With the current setup, the Cauldron people do the production of the cards themselves, since Drive Through Cards is apparently inexpensive enough for that to be viable.

Whereas developing a video game is shall we say more complicated logistically. You either need to be able to do all the work yourself, be independently wealthy enough to hire people to do it for you, or show to prospective outside funders that the project would be worth forking over enough dimes.

So I feel hoping for eventual Steam Workshop support is the best option as it makes the first two options more viable, since I'm afraid I just don't think the last option would be viable.

Or to sum up, I think folks making the request may possibly not be taking into account that "getting permission" is only half the matter; the other half is "finding the resources with which to do it once you have the permission".
